title: Definitions and conservative extensions: adding useful notation
summary: Eliminate defined relation and function symbols, construct unique model expansions, and prove that definitions create no new old-language theorems.
abstract: A name for doubling can make a calculation shorter without changing what arithmetic can prove. The same idea works in any first-order theory: a new relation can abbreviate a formula, and a new function can abbreviate a graph when the theory proves that every input has exactly one output. We construct formulas that remove these new symbols, including functions nested inside other terms. Every model of the original theory then has exactly one expansion satisfying the definitions. Soundness and completeness show that adding the definitions yields no new theorem in the original language. The conditions on function graphs explain why some apparently harmless definitions instead add assumptions.
